children.text: Impact on the Gen Z Demographic

In the past five years, Connor Wood, Nara Smith, Vanillamace, and Alix Earle have presented themselves through their own unique niches and have approached their content using their humour, personalities, and lifestyles. They’ve each built a strong following, all with different interests, but with the commonality of connecting with the Gen Z demographic. Giving space and a voice to this new generation of men and women, allowed them to grow into their own and strengthen their passions. In having an audience of such an influential age, they hold a lot of weight over the thoughts, actions, and feelings of their viewers.

The direct interactions that the influencers have with their audience creates a sense of community, allowing for a strong sense of loyalty to form. As the influencers impact on Gen Z grows, their own content targets the generation more, blurring the lines between the audience or the influencers impact on each other. Influencers’ actions affect the slang, the way people dress, buying patterns, and lifestyles of their audience. This has impacted the way newer generations navigate their own lifestyles and become aware of current societal trends. Additionally, the way influencers react to current political events, by staying silent or taking a stand, can shift the younger audience's perception and actions towards a certain issue. The influencers ability to understand and communicate with the audience causes them to become reliant on outside commentary. In the new age of Tiktok algorithms and quick cancellations, it is not possible for these influencers to block out the noise that comes from unintended audiences. Instead, they must lean into it.
Vanillamace Tries Her Hardest to Install a Wig

Vanillamace is a social media influencer and content creator whose personal brand revolves around her authentic personality, humour, relatability, and how she presents herself as an “unfiltered internet bestie”. Her content can be found across multiple platforms such as TikTok, Youtube, Instagram, and Twitch, with posts ranging from different niches such as beauty, fashion, gaming, shopping, and day in the life vlogs. Because she doesn’t stick to just one specific niche, her personality and interactions with her audience is what helps to connect her varying content. She stays active in live stream chats, which creates a sense of community and makes her videos feel as if being on facetime with a family member/friend. Beyond just entertainment, Vanillmace also uses her large platform to highlight political and social issues, including ICE and immigration policies, which reveals to her audience more of her personal values and character. Her unfiltered humour, self expression, and audience engagement all contribute to the relatable and authentic persona that she presents, contributing to her brand overall.

Alix Earle is a 25-year-old social media influencer with 8.7 million followers on Tiktok, with the majority of her followers being women between the ages 18-24. She originally gained popularity on the platform by documenting her life as a student at the University of Miami through her “Get Ready With Me” (GRWM) Tiktoks. She has since grown in immense popularity to be a dancer on Dancing With the Stars and her own reality show on Netflix, Earle Meets World. Her personal brand is centered on beauty, relationships, traveling, and details of her life. She has built a personal brand on unfiltered, conversational content that opposes typical polished images that most celebrities maintain. Her credibility comes from the trust and openness she has created with her viewers as she constantly updates on her personal experiences, from relationships to acne struggles. Alix has recently expanded her influence into entrepreneurship as she founded a skincare company, Reale Actives. Her transition from a college creator to internet celebrity demonstrates the multitude of opportunities an influencer’s personal identity could develop into a commercialized brand.

Nara Smith’s exposure to a low level of fame occurred long before she became an influencer. At just 14, Nara was discovered as a model which directly influenced her move to the US. Following this move, she met her husband Lucky and quickly started a family. In 2022, Nara posted a video after making bread and jam for her kids and following it’s virality she continued forward. Her persona developed overtime. While her style of video has diversified to some extent, most doom-scrollers would know her soothing voice, wild outfits, and outrageously lengthy recipes. Nara willingly talks about her branding and the backlash she’s received because of tradwife comparisons, but her actions are not always supportive of her own vision. Months before denying being a tradwife on Alex Cooper’s Call Her Daddy podcast, she spent extensive time with another influencer, Ballerina farm, who directly supports the tradwife narrative through her content. Overall, each one of Nara's videos provides imagery of an aesthetic luxury housewife lifestyle while creating just enough controversy to keep viewers engaged.
